title: perf-bench-scratch-rina-patel-2026-03-04
content:
Quick notes / scratchpad for perf runs (latency & throughput).

Date: 2026-03-04
Owner: Rina Patel
Hardware: 1x NVIDIA A100 80GB (node: dev-a100-17)
Model: llama-2-13b-chat (quantized: 8-bit (nf4), kv-cache enabled)
Serving binary: rw-serv-1.8.2 (commit: a7f3c2b)
Runner: bench/run_bench.py (internal)

Goal:
- Compare p50/p95 latency and QPS for small chat requests at different batching configs.
- Validate that KV prefix caching + continuous batching yields >= 2x throughput vs baseline for 1-4 concurrent clients.

Configs tested (high-level):
- baseline: batch=1, continuous_batching=false, kv_cache=false
- kb-cache: batch=1, continuous_batching=false, kv_cache=true
- cont-batch-small: batch=8, continuous_batching=true, max_tokens=128, kv_cache=true
- cont-batch-large: batch=32, continuous_batching=true, max_tokens=512, kv_cache=true

Commands (run locally on dev node):
- python bench/run_bench.py --model llama-2-13b --quantize nf4 --batch 1 --concurrent 4 --seq 128 --kv_cache false --out run_baseline.json
- python bench/run_bench.py --model llama-2-13b --quantize nf4 --batch 8 --concurrent 4 --seq 128 --kv_cache true --continuous true --out run_cont_small.json

Observed metrics (summary) -- runs pulled from bench results + Grafana spot checks:
- baseline (batch=1, kv=false)
  - qps: 7.2 req/s
  - tokens/s: ~1.8k tok/s
  - p50 latency: 135 ms
  - p95 latency: 480 ms

- kb-cache (batch=1, kv=true)
  - qps: 9.0 req/s
  - tokens/s: ~2.2k tok/s
  - p50 latency: 120 ms
  - p95 latency: 410 ms
  - notes: cold-start penalty for first request per prefix visible (~120ms extra)

- cont-batch-small (batch=8, continuous, kv=true)
  - qps: 18.5 req/s
  - tokens/s: ~4.5k tok/s
  - p50 latency: 170 ms (per-request, but amortized work higher)
  - p95 latency: 520 ms
  - GPU utilization: 68%
  - notes: throughput ~2.5x baseline; tail latency increases slightly but overall cost/token decreases.

- cont-batch-large (batch=32, continuous, kv=true, seq=512)
  - qps: 22.0 req/s
  - tokens/s: ~11.0k tok/s
  - p50 latency: 420 ms
  - p95 latency: 950 ms
  - GPU utilization: 92%
  - notes: best tokens/sec but per-request latency high for short prompts; good for batch workloads only.

Short ascii sparkline (tokens/sec across configs):
 baseline:  ████ (1.8k)
 kv-cache:  █████ (2.2k)
 cont-small: ██████████ (4.5k)
 cont-large: █████████████████ (11k)

Observations / quick conclusions:
- KV cache gives ~20-25% throughput improvement for short sequences due to reusing prefix KVs; cold-start overhead still a problem for first-turn interactive UX.
- Continuous batching increases total throughput significantly (2-6x depending on batch size) but shifts tail latency up; need per-route SLOs to decide trade-offs.
- For chat UIs with short prompts (<=128 tokens) and interactive SLAs, recommended defaults: continuous_batching=true, max_batch=8, kv_cache=true, latency_opt_mode on (experimental). This yields ~2x throughput with moderate p95 impact.
- For high-throughput offline scoring (long sequences), use batch sizes >=32 and allow higher p95.

Anomalies / things to investigate:
- p95 for cont-small is worse than expected vs baseline in one run (520ms vs expected ~450ms). Possibly due to background snapshot/GC on node dev-a100-17 at 11:02 UTC. Cross-check node logs: https://logs.redwood.internal/node/dev-a100-17/2026-03-04
- Memory fragmentation observed in nvidia-smi between cont runs (small increase in reserved memory). Might be quantization allocation path. File issue if reproducible.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Re-run cont-small at 3 different times of day to average out background noise (owners: Rina, Samira).
- Add micro-benchmark that isolates kv cache hit/miss cost (script: bench/kv_cache_profile.py).
- Try 4-bit quantization (nf4->4bit) on a single node to see perf delta and any quality regressions (coord with research).
- Add a Grafana panel that overlays qps + p95 + GPU utilization for quick triage (PR: serving-runtime/grafana#789).

Notes to self (non-final):
- If client latency budget <=200ms p95, avoid batch>8 for interactive routes.
- Document recommended defaults in product docs (product/hosted-api/perf-presets) once validated.

References / links:
- bench results: /data/bench/runs/2026-03-04/* (on internal NFS)
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abc123/throughput-dashboard
- Related Jira: RL-4321 (kv caching improvements)
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/789

End of scratchpad.

-- Rina
